title: SSE client-server chunk-granularity negotiation, deduplicated resume, and partial-functioncall reconciliation
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background:
We continue to see edge cases in long-running SSE sessions where network interruptions cause clients to reconnect and either replay duplicated chunks or irrevocably lose partial function-call payloads. Current resume token semantics are coarse-grained and assume chunk boundaries match server framing; they also rely on client-side heuristics for dedupe which have produced out-of-order function-call deliveries and duplicate tool invocations for a subset of customers.

Goals:
1) Provide a negotiated chunk granularity so clients and servers can agree on minimum resumable unit (byte-range vs logical event) to reduce ambiguous boundary splits.
2) Add light-weight stable chunk provenance identifiers to enable deduplication across reconnects without requiring heavy server-state per-client.
3) Define clear semantics for partial-functioncall reconciliation: allow clients to identify incomplete function-call frames, request server-side replay only for missing components, and avoid double-invoking tools.
4) Ensure backward compatibility: older clients must continue to work with the server (fall back path), and new clients should detect older servers and degrade to conservative semantics.

Design proposal (high level):
- Handshake: extend the initial SSE/subscribe handshake with an optional header 'x-rwd-sse-features: chunk-granularity=logical;checksum=sha256;resume-lease=60s'. The server returns 'x-rwd-sse-ack: chunk-granularity=byte:4096;resume-lease=30s' when it cannot offer logical granularity.
- Chunk provenance ID: each emitted chunk Event will include a provenance meta-field in the event payload (not as an extra SSE header to preserve compatibility) called "_prov": "<model>-<epoch>-<fragment-hash>". Fragment-hash is first 12 chars of sha256 over the chunk bytes and sequence metadata.
- Resume token: server issues resume tokens that anchor to the last acknowledged provenance ID plus a byte-offset within the provenance chunk. Resume token schema is opaque to clients but composed as base64("prov=<prov>|off=<n>|ts=<iso>").
- Deduplication: clients include last-seen provenance IDs when rejoining via 'x-rwd-last-provs: <prov>,<prov>'. Server uses these to avoid re-sending identical fragments; clients still perform local dedupe in case of incomplete delivery.
- Partial-functioncall reconciliation: when a tool/function-call node spans multiple chunks, each chunk includes a 'funccall_id' and a 'part_index' with 'part_count'. The server guarantees idempotent tool invocation only after all parts for funccall_id are acknowledged by the client. During resume, client will send 'x-rwd-request-missing: funccall_id=abc123' which instructs server to retransmit missing parts in canonical order. If server does not have state (e.g., after lease expiry), it will reply with 'x-rwd-missing-mode: replay-only' and include the complete function-call envelope as a new event with a new prov ID.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Putting prov ID inside the event payload keeps older clients functioning (they ignore the extra field). However, it slightly increases payload size and requires consumer parsing.
- Server-side resume-lease reduces indefinite server memory usage but introduces a window where resumed clients must accept a heavier replay. We set conservative defaults (30s) and expose tuning via dedicated deployments.
- Requiring client inclusion of last-provs during reconnect reduces server work for dedupe but relies on clients to persist that short-lived state. Mobile and ephemeral clients need guidance in docs.

API compatibility and fallback paths:
- If server does not advertise 'chunk-granularity' or 'prov' capabilities, clients must revert to current resume tokens and conservative heuristics (replay last N events).
- New servers will accept older clients: when client doesn't send 'x-rwd-last-provs' server will publish full chunks until an explicit ack range is received.

Operational concerns and metrics:
- New metrics to track: resume-success-rate, duplicate-chunk-rate, incomplete-funcall-replays, average-resume-latency, prov-collision-count (should be near zero).
- Rollout strategy: stage on internal canary cluster -> dedicated customers that opt-in -> default behavior after 4 weeks. Monitor duplicate-chunk-rate and tool double-invoke incident rate during rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Resume flows: end-to-end resume with last-prov included succeeds in at least 99.5% of simulated flaky-network tests without duplicated function-call invocation.
- Backcompat: older clients (at least 2 previous SDK versions) can connect and receive a stream with no protocol errors.
- Performance: CPU and memory overhead introduced by prov-id hashing remains below 3% at p95 load.

QA and testing plan:
- Unit tests for prov ID generation and resume token encoding/decoding.
- Integration harness that simulates byte-level cuts in the middle of function-call frames and ensures reconcile protocol prevents duplicates.
- Chaos test: randomized reconnects across NAT boundaries and mobile clients, validate dedupe and funcall idempotency.

Rollout and docs:
- Update SDKs to persist last-provs in reconnect path and surface the 'x-rwd-sse-features' handshake parsing.
- Confluence design doc with diagrams (link below) describing seq diagrams for normal stream, abrupt cut, and resume path.
- Migration guide for customers describing tuning knobs (resume-lease, chunk-granularity preference).
comments: 2026-02-28 - Triage: flagged as P0 after two customer incidents where a tool was invoked twice during reconnects. Assigned to Marcus Li.

2026-03-03 - Design review: Product and Runtime Eng reviewed. Requested stronger guarantees around idempotency for external tool adapters; suggested adding server-side idempotency tokens for long-lived adapters.
2026-03-05 - Engineering note: prototype of prov-id encoding implemented in branch feat/sse-provenance (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123). Basic tests for prov collisions added.
2026-03-10 - Security review: initial pass — no new secrets introduced. Confirmed prov is non-sensitive. Security requested limits on resume-lease length which was accepted.
2026-03-14 - Current: working on client SDK changes (python/js) to persist last-provs and send x-rwd-last-provs during reconnect. Integration tests scheduled for 2026-03-18.
